verdict.label: NEUTRAL
verdict.title: The market is expensive and volatile: a well-managed PVPC still wins
verdict.body: With a 90-day average of 155 €/MWh (+72.9% vs the previous period), the pool price has surged. For a typical household (270 kWh/month), the estimated PVPC bill is around 56 €/month. There are not yet enough fixed tariffs in the database to compare against: once they appear, we will recompute the verdict.

factors.title: Wind keeps driving midday prices down
factors.body: Days with maximum wind generation register lows below marginal cost. On 23/08 the pool hit -2.10 €/MWh at midday: producing in those hours (or not consuming) is the biggest savings lever.

factors.title: Spikes up to 380 €/MWh in peak electricity hours
factors.body: On 04/11 the price peaked at 380 €/MWh at 20:00, with a daily average of 257.55 €/MWh. Under PVPC that hour costs about 0.47 €/kWh: skipping the washing machine and oven in peak hours saves more than any tariff.

factors.title: The mid-price band was the cheapest of the quarter
factors.body: Average PVPC price by band over the last 90 days: off-peak 0.217 €/kWh, mid-peak 0.199 €/kWh and peak 0.208 €/kWh. Shifting consumption to the mid-price band (late morning and end of afternoon) is the easiest and most profitable optimisation.
factors.impact: Direct impact: mid-peak 9% cheaper than off-peak

golden_rule: Shift consumption to the mid-price band: it was the cheapest of the quarter (0.20 €/kWh vs 0.22 in off-peak).
